**Issue #1989 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1989: Patch: who takes the first turn of an online match is the match seed's coin, not who queued first or who hosts, and a rematch swaps the seats
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today the first turn of an online game always goes to the same side: whoever joined the queue first, whoever made the room, and in a rematch the same player as last time, game after game. Against a ladder bot the person always goes first. After this, a coin drawn from each match's seed decides who goes first, the same coin every replay draws, and a rematch hands the first turn to the other player. Nobody can choose the first turn any more by queueing early or by hosting. The ladder bots also start playing from the first seat, so their ratings stop being measured from one seat only.

## Why

The spec gives the first turn to Player 1 (§2.1 step 5). The server always seats the same person there:

- **Queue.** `try_pair` sorts the open tickets oldest first (`crates/server/src/api/queue.rs:668`). The outer ticket `a` becomes `PlayerId::P1` (`queue.rs:759`, `start_paired_match` at `:553-571`). §9.5 states it: "between two people the older ticket is Player 1".
- **Rooms.** The host is always P1 (`crates/server/src/actor/rooms.rs:241-279`).
- **Rematches.** `finished.players.0` is P1 again (`crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs:224-243`). That includes double-or-nothing, which doubles the rating move (R672).
- **Bots.** R1453 seats the person as P1 every time. It rejected a coin because a coin "would put a lone player second half the time, which no pairing with a person does". That reason is only consistency with the older-ticket rule; a coin for every pairing removes it.
- **Conquest.** R335 makes the player who queued first, or hosted, the series' p1, who goes first in the odd games. So a three-game series also leans the same way.

The seat matters to the owner. R1156000 raised Player 1's opening draw "for seat balance" (issue #1156). R335 alternates series games so the first seat is not "a prize". Live ladder-bot ratings (R610) are fitted only on games where the bot sits second. The offline calibration, by contrast, alternates seats (`docs/bot-calibration.md:29-30`).

## Proposal

- Draw the seats from the match seed on a stream of their own, with a named label as `dealt_deck`'s seat deals have. This applies at every 1v1 door: queue pairs (Best of 1 and All Random), room joins and bot pairings.
- A rematch swaps the seats of the match it follows.
- A Conquest series draws its p1 by the same coin and keeps R335's alternation.
- End-to-end runs get a seat override beside R143's seed override, so the seeded e2e specs keep the seats they were written for.
- A new ruling in the issue's own block amends R1453, R335 and §9.5.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/api/queue.rs`, `crates/server/src/actor/rooms.rs`, `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs`, the bot pairing path (`crates/server/src/bots/`) and the series start (`crates/server/src/api/series*.rs`)
- `crates/server/src/config.rs` (the stream's label)
- The server tests that assume host or older ticket is P1, and the seeded e2e room specs
- `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.5 and §9.12, `spec/rulings/R1453.md`, `spec/rulings/R0335.md`, a new ruling note, `spec/INDEX.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Over a fixed set of seeds, a queue pair, a room and a bot pairing each produce both seat orders, and the same seed always gives the same seats.
- [ ] A rematch (and a double-or-nothing) seats the previous match's P2 as P1.
- [ ] A Conquest series' first game follows the coin and its games still alternate (R335's tests, amended).
- [ ] Each e2e spec seats as it was written, through the end-to-end override.
- [ ] A new match's replay folds to its hash; `cargo jackioh spec check` is green with the new ruling.

## Size and risks

Hard: a design change across the server, a ruling and many tests (about 16 server files assume who sits first). Whether the first seat should be a coin at all is the owner's decision; Hearthstone tosses one. No engine rule changes, since Player 1 still goes first. The client already reads who goes first from the view.
```
